Inference for a difference in differences with few clusters

Source: R/wcbx.R
wcbx.Rd

Tests of the two-way fixed-effects effect of didfe() that stay accurate when a policy was assigned to a handful of clusters (districts, states), where the cluster-robust t test over-rejects: the restricted wild cluster bootstrap, and the permutation of the adoption dates across clusters; and the power of a design simulated on real untreated data.

Usage

wcbx(
  y,
  unit,
  time,
  trt = NULL,
  adj = NULL,
  clus = NULL,
  meth = "wild",
  reps = NULL,
  wtype = "rad",
  ties = "count",
  stat = "t",
  ntrt = 1,
  adopt = NULL,
  eff = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  power = 0.8,
  seed = NULL,
  level = 0.95
)

Arguments

y

The outcome: numbers, one per row; for meth = "perm" also a matrix or data frame of several outcomes, one column each.

unit

The unit of each row: labels.

time

The period of each row: numbers (a year, a month index); each unit at most once per period.

trt

The treatment of each row, 0 or 1 ("wild", "perm"; for "perm" it must stay on, from one period within each cluster); NULL for "power".

adj

NULL or time-varying controls: a data frame or list of columns, a numeric matrix, or one vector, one value per row. Factor, text and logical columns enter as indicators of each level but the first.

clus

NULL (cluster by unit) or the cluster of each row.

meth

"wild", "perm" or "power".

reps

The draws: a whole number from 9; NULL for 9999 (200 for "power").

wtype

"rad" (Rademacher) or "webb".

ties

"count" or "strict".

stat

"t" or "est": the statistic permuted.

ntrt

The clusters treated in each power draw.

adopt

The adoption periods drawn from, periods of time.

eff

NULL (0 to two standard deviations of y in five steps) or the effects tried.

alpha

The level of the power test.

power

The power of the minimum detectable effect.

seed

The seed of the draws: NULL to draw it from R's generator, or a whole number from 0.

level

The confidence level of the intervals: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

Value

An object of class wcbx, a list: res, for "wild" one row (est, stat, p, lo, hi), for "perm" one row per outcome (outcome, est, stat, p, pstep), for "power" one row per effect (eff, power); meth; ncl; draws; enum (TRUE when every draw was enumerated); mde and size ("power", else NA); and level.

Details

meth = "wild" is the restricted wild cluster bootstrap-t (WCR) of Cameron, Gelbach and Miller (2008): the model is fitted with the null b = b0 imposed, each bootstrap outcome is that fit plus its residuals multiplied cluster by cluster by a random sign (wtype = "rad") or one of Webb's six values ("webb"), and the CR1 t statistic of didfe() is recomputed. The p-value is the share of draws with |t*| at least |t| (ties = "count": the sign patterns that reproduce the data are among the draws, as the observed assignment is in a permutation test) or above it ("strict", as 'fwildclusterboot' counts). With Rademacher weights and 2^G <= reps every sign pattern is enumerated. The interval collects the b0 not rejected at 1 - level, by bisection with the same draws; with Rademacher weights the smallest attainable p-value is 2 / 2^G, so with four clusters nothing is rejected at 5% and the interval is the whole line: the honest answer.

meth = "perm" shuffles the adoption period of each cluster (all its units adopt together; never is a period too) among the clusters, keeping the number adopting at each date, and recomputes the t statistic (stat = "t") or the estimate ("est"). When the distinct assignments number at most reps they are all enumerated and p is the exact share at least as extreme; otherwise p = (b + 1) / (R + 1) over R random ones. The test is Fisher's: valid in any sample when the dates were assigned at random. With several outcomes (the columns of y), pstep holds the Westfall-Young stepdown p-values of wystep() over the same assignments.

meth = "power" draws ntrt clusters, gives each an adoption period drawn from adopt, adds each effect of eff to their outcomes from adoption on, and counts the CR1 t tests that reject at alpha; on real untreated data the serial correlation and clustering are carried, as formula-based power calculations do not (Burlig, Preonas and Woerman 2020). size is the rejection rate at effect 0 (it should be near alpha); mde, where the power curve first crosses power, by linear interpolation.

References

Cameron, A. C., Gelbach, J. B. and Miller, D. L. (2008). Bootstrap-based improvements for inference with clustered errors. Review of Economics and Statistics, 90(3), 414-427. doi:10.1162/rest.90.3.414

Webb, M. D. (2023). Reworking wild bootstrap-based inference for clustered errors. Canadian Journal of Economics, 56(3), 839-858. doi:10.1111/caje.12661

Burlig, F., Preonas, L. and Woerman, M. (2020). Panel data and experimental design. Journal of Development Economics, 144, 102458. doi:10.1016/j.jdeveco.2020.102458

Examples

d <- expand.grid(year = 2015:2024, town = LETTERS[1:8])
i <- match(d$town, LETTERS)
d$bylaw <- as.integer(i <= 3 & d$year >= 2019)
d$rate <- 30 + i + 0.5 * (d$year - 2015) - 2 * d$bylaw + sin(seq_len(80))
# eight towns: every one of the 2^8 sign patterns
wcbx(d$rate, d$town, d$year, d$bylaw)
#> wcbx: wild, 8 clusters, 256 draws (all enumerated)
#>        est      stat         p        lo        hi
#>  -1.987082 -9.207341 0.0078125 -2.524054 -1.431829
# every assignment of the by-law to three of the eight towns
wcbx(d$rate, d$town, d$year, d$bylaw, meth = "perm")$res
#>   outcome       est      stat          p      pstep
#> 1      y1 -1.987082 -9.207341 0.01785714 0.01785714
